visualReview.notes: Inspected all 13 current portable frames after the 851,816-triangle revision: lit preview, four turntable views, both complete elevations, distant silhouette, lower jali and carvings, stepped shaft, balconies/cornices, upper pavilions and ribbed crown. The revised upper shaft widths, two open pavilion levels, corner piers, brackets, curved ribbed crown, clear south entrance and recessed jali match the documented exterior hierarchy. The source has coherent exterior surfaces, connected stair/terrace and visible relief depth without clipping or duplicate panel surfaces. Small carvings use original polygonal representations; close detail cameras intentionally crop the overall tower.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all 13 current shared-surface frames with sky reflections: four full angles, eight named cameras and the north-up geographic placement frame. The continuous shared sandstone material retains metric grain and vertex tint across the stepped shaft, terrace, reliefs, pavilions and roof without artificial extra masonry courses. Complete south and north views contain the entire tower. Geographic load and unload assertions passed.

geographicReview.notes: The exact-identity OpenStreetMap way 1549061397, identified by its monument name and exact en:Vijaya Stambha article, supplies the tower center and square roof axis. Its August 2026 outline is the roughly 5.8 m upper roof rather than the 14.32 m ground terrace; the model therefore uses its center and directed axis without shrinking the documented base. The ASI north-arrow plan independently identifies the southern entrance. Native +Z follows that entrance, with heading 0.026694748787334657 radians and anchor [74.645123975,24.887826525]. The current north-up placement frame agrees with this registration and reviewed terrain-contact placement. No unverified absolute elevation is implied.

fidelityReview.notes: Passed for the detailed world-viewer exterior reconstruction after comparison with the ASI plan and dimensions reproduced in UNESCO nomination 247rev, official Rajasthan Tourism current photographs, and primary north/southwest/entrance archival photographs. Published 37.19 m height, 14.32 m maximum support and nine levels govern the asset; the separately documented approximately 30 ft tower body, stepped cross, broad lower two levels, five narrower closed levels, expanded eighth and smaller ninth open pavilions, deeply projecting mouldings, cardinal balcony windows, entrance jali and ribbed crown are represented. Intermediate levels and restored crown curvature remain explicitly proportional reconstruction. Original shallow reliefs preserve the observed density and human/pilaster/floral vocabulary without pretending to reproduce every deity attribute, damaged inscription or carving face. These localized reconstruction limits do not omit the visible exterior components required for this asset. The independently resolved mapped roof center and ASI south entrance now support the separately passed geographic review.
